text: Updating the hottest headlines in
today's program. Authorities suspected
of covering up a disease outbreak.
Nearly 200 people quarantined in
Siberia due to a mysterious, dangerous
illness reminiscent of the early days
of Wuhan. The epidemic in Siberia could
pose a threat to China. Beijing remains
silent regarding the unusual
developments. Chinese shoulder-fired
missile weapons unexpectedly appear in
the hands of Russian troops. Is Beijing
crossing the red line? Ukraine pierces
the Russian defensive line. Heavy
battle tanks return; Challenger 2 makes
an appearance. Zelensky hints at a
bridge strike. We have our own programs
and activities, along with many
noteworthy pieces of information that
we will update in today's broadcast.
Right now, we invite you to follow the
detailed information. Hoai Phuong
welcomes the audience watching the
Russia-Ukraine news bulletin, updated
daily on HTD News channel. Ladies and
gentlemen, an unusual medical
development is causing concern in the
Siberia region as nearly 200 people
have been quarantined following the
death of a female employee at a
facility specializing in research on
highly dangerous infectious diseases.
Ladies and gentlemen, according to
information published by The Sun, the
deceased is Daria Sibilova, 28, an
employee of the plague research
institute. She is believed to have
fallen ill after an expedition near the
Russia-Mongolia border, then was
hospitalized in Sorsk and passed away.
What makes the incident particularly
sensitive is that the Russian
authorities are implementing very
strict epidemic prevention measures but
have not publicly confirmed the exact
disease. Governor Igor Kobzev only
described it as a dangerous infectious
disease. According to the published
figures, at least 189 people have been
quarantined or monitored, with over 100
quarantined at a hospital, dozens at
another facility, and 12 being
monitored at the plague research
institute. Some cases are reported to
have already shown symptoms. Notably,
the head of the Russian health watchdog
Rospotrebnadzor, Anna Popova, also
rushed to the scene. But so far, the
most important question still has no
clear answer. What is the actual
pathogen? It is this information vacuum
that has led the British press to
compare the situation to the early days
of the Covid-19 pandemic in Wuhan.
Control measures have been tightened
and contacts have been quarantined, but
information regarding the nature of the
pathogen remains very limited.
According to reports, an advisory
warning Bancas residents to avoid
Celecop also reportedly disappeared
from official sources shortly after.
Meanwhile, Russian media has floated a
hypothesis about a test tube containing
bacteria breaking inside a laboratory.
However, epidemiologist Mhan Favopov
questioned this scenario, arguing that
laboratories handling dangerous
pathogens maintain very strict safety
protocols. He also raised the
possibility that the patient initially
had respiratory problems and was
misdiagnosed, which may have delayed
appropriate antibiotic treatment.
Dear viewers, these are still just
hypotheses, so the biggest concern
right now is not to assume Russia is
facing a plague outbreak as such
information is not officially confirmed
. What is concerning is that nearly 200
people have already been forced into
quarantine. A young expert has died,
and a high-ranking health official from
Moscow had to immediately fly to
Siberia while authorities have yet to
clearly disclose the disease they are
dealing with. In a medical incident
involving a dangerous pathogen, silence
does not make the fear disappear. It
only leads to bigger questions about
what is actually happening in EOS. The
epidemic in Siberia could pose a threat
to China. Beijing remains silent in the
face of these unusual developments.
Ladies and gentlemen, the mysterious
outbreak in Siberia has just seen a
notable new development. According to
information cited by Russian media, the
death of a 28-year-old female worker in
the EUS region has been confirmed by a
Russian official as related to the
plague. Meanwhile, about 200 people who
potentially came into contact with the
patient are being monitored. Especially
concerning is the suspicion regarding
pneumonic plague, the most dangerous
form, because unlike bubonic plague, it
can spread from person to person
through droplets during close contact.
Dear viewers, epidemic prevention
measures in IUS are therefore being
strengthened. A quarantine order has
been implemented in XOP. Mask-wearing
is also being enforced at the local
aluminum smelter, while the head of
Rospotrebnadzor, Anna Popova, has
traveled directly to the region and an
emergency meeting on epidemic
prevention was held. But a new question
has emerged. If this is truly pneumonic
plague, will the risk be contained
within Russia? Yekaterinburg does not
directly border China, but a
significant network of trade, tourism,
and travel exists between this region
and China. A Chinese consulate is
located right in the city. Chinese
citizens and businesses operate in the
region, while tourists and business
people frequently travel between the
two countries. More importantly, travel
between Russia and China is currently
relatively convenient, making the flow
of people, rather than just
geographical distance, the primary
concern. Yet, at the time of reporting,
Beijing has not announced any special
control measures regarding the incident
. No border closures, no new travel
restrictions, and no significant
additional quarantine measures for
travelers from the affected area have
been introduced. This may simply
reflect a current assessment that the
situation is under control, but
everything could change if more
infections emerge among the nearly 200
people under surveillance. According to
the World Health Organization, plague
is caused by the bacterium Yersinia
pestis and can be treated with
antibiotics if detected early.
Pneumonic plague, in particular, can
progress very rapidly and spread
between people through close contact.
Dear viewers, therefore, the decisive
question now is not whether China needs
to close its borders immediately, but
how many people the deceased woman had
contact with, whether secondary
transmission has occurred, and exactly
what form of the disease Russia is
facing. If no further cases appear,
this may just be a localized outbreak.
But if a chain of transmission has
already begun, what is happening in
Siberia will no longer be just
Russia’s own story. Chinese
shoulder-fired missile weapons have
unexpectedly appeared in the hands of
Russian troops. Is Beijing crossing a
red line? Ladies and gentlemen, an
unusual detail has just appeared on
Russian state television, raising new
questions about the extent of China's
military support for Moscow. Ladies and
gentlemen, according to Spigo, in a
report by the Rossiya 1 channel in the
Rostov region, a Russian soldier
showcased a man-portable air-defense
system that looks very similar to
China's QW-18 or QW-19. Notably, these
are not the familiar Russian Igla or
Verba systems. In the footage, the
soldier holds the system, points it
toward the sky, and states that the
weapon can engage targets at a range of
about 4 km. This unit is tasked with
protecting Russian facilities from
Ukrainian UAVs, which makes the
appearance of this weapon particularly
notable. Increasingly deep Ukrainian
UAV strikes are forcing Russia to
disperse a large number of air defense
systems to protect airfields, defense
plants, fuel depots, energy facilities,
and targets located deep in the rear.
If the Russian Ministry of Defense is
indeed incorporating Chinese-origin
systems into its defensive network, it
could indicate that the pressure on
Russia's air defense capabilities is so
great that the Kremlin must seek
additional external supplies. China's
QW-18 is an infrared-guided
man-portable air-defense missile
designed to counter low-flying targets.
According to the public specifications
cited in the article, the system has an
operational range of about 5 km and can
engage targets at altitudes of up to 4
km. However, there is one point that
requires particular caution. To
accurately determine the origin of the
system that appeared in Rostov, at
least three possibilities are being
considered. The weapon was supplied
directly by China, it was transferred
to Russia via a third country, or
Russia possesses a system produced
under license or based on a similar
design. There is not yet enough
published evidence to conclude which
scenario is correct. But if subsequent
investigations confirm that these are
indeed Chinese missiles supplied by
Beijing to the Russian military, the
political implications would be
significant. Because until now, China
has maintained its official position
that it does not provide lethal weapons
to Russia in the Ukraine war. Dear
viewers, Chinese components appearing
in Russian weapons is one thing,
dual-use equipment is another, but a
complete air defense missile system in
the hands of the Russian military would
be a completely different story. And
that is why what seemed like a normal
piece of footage from Russian
television is now posing a very
difficult question for Beijing. Is this
just a system that resembles Chinese
weaponry, or is it the first sign that
a line in Russia-China military
relations has truly been crossed?
Ukraine pierces Russian defensive lines
. Heavy tanks return. Challenger 2
appears. Dear viewers, a very notable
development is emerging on the
Ukrainian battlefield. After a period
where heavy tanks had to operate with
extreme caution due to dense drone
activity, the Ukrainian military is
reportedly bringing armor back to the
front lines, exploiting Russian
defensive areas that have just been
breached. Ladies and gentlemen,
according to The Telegraph, what is
notable is not merely the appearance of
tanks, but that Ukraine spent months
preparing the battlefield before moving
them in. In the area near
Oleshky-Prymorske, Ukrainian forces
reportedly conducted an
eight-month-long campaign aimed at
striking links behind the Russian
defensive lines. Supply routes were
attacked, and logistics convoys were
hunted down. Russian communications
were exploited for targeting, and
specifically, Russian drone operator
crews near the front lines became
priority targets for Ukrainian unmanned
aerial vehicles. When the enemy's drone
network and logistics were pushed back
or weakened, Ukrainian infantry
advanced, and only then did the tanks
appear. According to the report,
armored vehicles use heavy firepower to
strike Russian defensive positions,
supporting infantry to expand the
breakthrough and, more importantly,
helping to hold the areas just
recaptured. Challenger 2 tanks provided
by the UK are believed to be among the
vehicles participating in these
operations. Ukraine is reported to have
recaptured about 745 km² around the
Oleksandrivka area, although specific
developments in each area still need
further monitoring. A similar tactic
has also appeared in Avdiivka and
Kharkiv. Unit 9.2 released footage of
two tanks equipped with anti-drone
systems entering combat, supported by
reconnaissance drones and heavy Vampire
unmanned aerial vehicles. The tanks
carried out hit-and-run strikes, using
their main guns to attack buildings
where Russian infantry were hiding
before withdrawing. According to the
unit, both vehicles returned safely.
Ladies and gentlemen, this is not yet
the return of formations with dozens of
tanks charging across the front line.
As seen in previous wars. On the
contrary, it shows that tanks must
adapt to a completely new battlefield.
To deploy a Challenger 2 or any heavy
tank, one must first employ
reconnaissance drones, electronic
warfare, infantry, and long-range fire
to blind, disrupt logistics, and push
enemy drones out of the operational
zone. Once those conditions are met,
thick armor and large-caliber guns
become an advantage again. Therefore,
the lesson from Oleksandrivka is not
that tanks have defeated drones, but
that they have become more dangerous to
Russian forces. Ukraine is learning how
to hunt the enemy's eyes first before
bringing in tanks to exploit the gaps
that drones and infantry have opened.
Zelenskyy hints at a strike on the
Kerch Bridge. We have our own plans and
operations. Ladies and gentlemen,
following Russian attacks on Ukraine's
bridges and transport infrastructure,
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has just
sent a notable message: Kyiv will
retaliate. And when asked directly
whether the bridge connecting Russia to
the Crimean peninsula was on the target
list, Mr. Zelenskyy neither confirmed
nor denied it. The President of Ukraine
replied: "We have our own plans, our
own steps, and our own operations that
align with the tasks and priorities of
our defense forces." Ladies and
gentlemen, this was a very deliberate
answer. Mr. Zelenskyy did not disclose
targets, timing, or means of attack,
but he made it clear that Russian
strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure
would not go unanswered. And Kyiv has
established criteria for selecting
targets: facilities of military and
logistical significance, especially
routes used by Russia to transport
troops, weapons, equipment, and
resources for the war effort. If viewed
through that lens, the question
regarding the Kerch Bridge immediately
becomes sensitive. This bridge holds
not only symbolic significance for the
Kremlin, but it is also a vital
transport route connecting Russian
territory to Crimea, facilitating the
movement of people and goods to the
peninsula. Therefore, Mr. Zelensky's
refusal to speak specifically about the
bridge, while immediately emphasizing
military and logistical facilities,
will certainly catch Moscow's attention
. This message comes at a time when
Ukraine is increasingly demonstrating
its ability to carry the war deeper
into the Russian rear. Oil and gas
facilities, refineries, airfields,
ammunition depots, and centers serving
the Russian military industry have
continuously become targets of
long-range campaigns. Meanwhile,
Ukraine is also developing new attack
capabilities, from long-range UAVs and
cruise missiles to a domestic ballistic
missile program. This makes the
challenge of protecting Russia's rear
increasingly complex. Mr. Zelensky
simultaneously dismissed the image of
the Kremlin genuinely seeking peace.
According to the Ukrainian President,
what Vladimir Putin is doing shows that
Moscow is choosing to escalate rather
than prepare to end the war. Mr.
Zelensky emphasized that this is not a
person ready to end the war. This is
not a peace-loving person, and thus,
his answer regarding the Kerch Bridge
is perhaps noteworthy precisely because
of what he did not say. But Kyiv also
did not say that the bridge would be
excluded. The message was, instead,
very brief. If Russia strikes Ukrainian
logistics, then the logistics routes
serving Russia's war machine cannot
automatically be considered a safe zone
. And that information concludes this
news bulletin from HTD News. Thank you
for watching. See you in the next
bulletins.
